audits.mathematicalReason: There are C(12,2)=66 games, each awarding exactly 2 points, so the team scores sum to 132. An even sum requires an even number of odd scores; because there are 12 teams, the number of even scores is also even. Two zero-score teams are impossible because their mutual game awards points to at least one of them. The total is certainly at least 100. However, if every game is drawn, every team scores 11, disproving E. The double count, parity reasoning, and counterexample scopes are all defensible.

routes.label: Color a cycle using endpoint states

audits.mathematicalReason: The forbidden-equality graph is the labeled cycle A−C−E−B−D−A. A color class has at most two vertices, so the possible multiplicity patterns are five singletons, one pair and three singletons, or two pairs and one singleton. Their counts are respectively P(6,5)=720, 5·P(6,4)=1800, and 5·P(6,3)=600. The factors of 5 count allowable single pairs and allowable disjoint pair patterns. The total is 3120. A recurrence tracking equality with the first cycle color also gives 5⁵−5=3120. Both v01 and v02 provide defensible alternative routes, with no identification under rotations or reflections.
